answer: A botanical garden gives each agent one lotus pond to tend. Every dawn the keeper counts the open blooms and weighs the nectar the bees carried in, dropping it into a walnut shell cup marked with the pond number. A pond with copied counts or an empty cup loses its bed for a season, and only ponds with three straight seasons of matching counts earn a harvest share. A thousand fake ponds need a thousand dawn counts, a thousand weighed cups, and a thousand seasons of real blooms.
